modes.label: Maximum dose phrases
modes.description: Fires on 'recommended' or 'human' following 'maximum' in dose limits.
modes.example: In patients with moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 7 to 9), the maximum<< recommended>> dosage is phentermine and topiram

modes.label: Max in dosing shorthand
modes.description: Fires on the number or space after '(max' in dose expressions.

modes.label: Highest level allowed
modes.description: Fires where a ceiling on a quantity is described, as in limits or constants.
modes.example: is the highest level of a contamin<<ant>> allowed in drinking water.

card.writes: It pushes toward words like 'allowed' and 'permitted' and away from 'minimum' and 'at least'.
card.plain: It marks spots where text is describing an upper limit, such as a maximum dose.
